biggestGap: elemental-large has no material identity: it is one smooth gray gem-loft torso with pencil-thin mannequin arms and a featureless sphere head, while every one of the 14 elemental references builds the body FROM the element (3-6 overlapping rock plates or flame tongues per limb) with oversized claw-mass hands and strong value breaks inside the body. Ours reads as a floating jewelry display, not an elemental.
notes: DRAGON (rest) vs WoW black drake: reference wins. The folded wing does not read as arm + wrist spike + finger struts + sag — at sheet distance it reads as a stegosaurus back-sail; only the face close-up hints at a folded membrane. The drake's folded-wing anatomy dominates its silhouette; ours could be a spined lizard with no wings at all in the silhouette panel. DRAGON-WALK (spread) vs drake: reference wins. The spread wing is NOT one continuous membrane — 3/4, front, and top panels all show disjoint triangular flags with visible gaps between the inner panel and the wrist fan, like a broken umbrella; the drake's membrane is one unbroken sheet from body to wingtip with sag between struts. Body, legs, and head carriage under the wings are actually decent in the walk side panel. SERPENT vs Valheim serpent: reference wins on menace and surface. Our croc-jaw face close-up with fangs and red maw is respectable, but the body is a smooth tube with a token red dorsal ridge versus Valheim's heavy dorsal spikes, scale value texture, and tooth-bristled jaw. Note: the front panel shows THREE stacked heads and 3/4 shows two — if this fixture is a single-headed serpent that is a duplicated-head generator artifact, not a style choice; flagging as possible harness/generator bug. OOZE vs shipped slimes (no ref image on disk, judged from knowledge of Dragon Quest / Slime Rancher / Minecraft slimes as instructed): closest call on the wall — the translucent teal shell over a darker interior core genuinely reads as gel and beats a flat blob. But it has no anchor feature (no eye ring, mouth, or core highlight a shipped slime always carries) and the silhouette is a formless pile; a hesitant tie is a loss. BEAST-LARGE (random roll) vs Valheim boar: reference wins big. Ours is exactly the flagged naked-doll failure: uniform gray, zero surface value variation, camel-long sausage neck, snake head with cartoon yellow eyes; the boar carries shoulder mass vs haunch contrast, bristle silhouette, and countershading. CELESTIAL-LARGE (random roll) vs Valheim greydwarf brute: reference wins big. Ours is a beige mannequin with a feather fan sprouting from the hip/lower back that reads as a turkey tail, not wings; wings sit below the shoulder line and vanish in the front view. The brute has integrated limbs, material identity, and a face; ours has two dot eyes on an egg. ELEMENTAL-LARGE (random roll) vs the 14-image elemental bar: catastrophic loss — see biggestGap. No plates, no tongues, no claw hands, no value breaks, no face zone; it violates every line of DESIGN-LANGUAGE.md at once. HARNESS FLAGS: (1) ooze 3/4/front panels are framed with the horizon at the very top so the subject sits low-contrast against solid grass — framing bug, not art; (2) elemental-large face panel is a full-frame featureless sphere — if the camera is aimed at a head that has no features that is an art fail, but the framing gives no context to tell; (3) serpent multi-head noted above; (4) reference library housekeeping: the contents of water-elemental-tall-splash.webp and magma-vs-ice-pair.jpg appear swapped relative to their filenames. VERDICT LOGIC: dragon-walk membrane and both random rolls (celestial, elemental) are unshippable; wall loses.
